top.title: Bombshell report details rift between Bayern Munich, Jamal Musiala’s management
top.description: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images An explosive report from German outlet Stern (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) details the growing schism between Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management. If true, Bayern Munich’s decision to go public and en gage in this fracas through the media sti ll loo ks bad, though there do appear to be issues with transparency and understanding from both sides, along with a total lack of a plan for how to move forward. The report goes back to last season and points to Musiala having a seizure on April 7, the day Bayern Munich played Real Madrid in the Champions League: A @sternde team conducted intensive research into the Jamal Musiala case in recent weeks and spoke with numerous people close to the club. The emerging picture revealed a veritable power struggle between the club’s management and Musiala’s representatives, involving new information, mistrust, and suspicion Here are the main points/results of the investigation: -Musiala suffered a lapse four days before his return to training, which was initially kept from the public by Bayern’s sporting management and the player’s management. The club’s higher ups only learned of it later in the week and were annoyed -Musiala also suffered an absence seizure on the morning of the Real Madrid game on April 7th while in a Madrid hotel. He was later subbed on in the game. What Musiala’s entourage considers a normal and manageable part of everyday life for someone with a neurological dysfunction is said to have infuriated some of the club’s bosses – because they were allegedly not informed about the player’s lapses at all, or only informed later -Some of the bosses now believe that the player’s management is withholding something crucial from them, that something is being covered up, and that the player’s health could be in a worse state than they are being told -@sternde confronted Jamal Musiala’s management with these and other questions. The player’s representatives stated that they would not comment on individual medical incidents. The agency added that they maintain a good and constructive dialogue with Bayern’s sporting management. FC Bayern also declined to comment for legal reasons -Bayern bosses are concerned that Musiala is allowed to choose his own doctors, while the club is kept in the dark. The concern also includes the fact that Musiala’s camp explicitly negotiated a much longer period of sick pay than usual, which seemed dubious given the illness – because the contract was signed before the diagnosis was made public. The bosses are now suspecting that they may have been taken advantage of Health aside, the massive financial stake in the player (potential €150 million total package through 2030) has the club concerned. top.title: 2027: Zamfara people firmly behind APC despite insults, criticism — Yari
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, says the people of Zamfara are firmly behind the party despite criticism and what he called insults directed at it. Yari spoke on Monday at the APC governorship campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara, Zamfara State. He said the turnout showed the party had the support it needed to win elections at every level in 2027. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly,” Yari said. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party.” Supporters gathered at the town’s Eid ground for the rally after welcoming Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara, according to the report. Lawal thanked the crowd and praised supporters for their solidarity, resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. “Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude,” he said, adding, “At this point, I will simply say, Let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day.” The APC campaign train is expected to visit other local government areas in Zamfara as the party continues its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. top.title: Russia launches Progress cargo ship to the International Space Station
top.description: null Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station. The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long. The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module. The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019. Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com. Progress 96 cargo spacecraft packed with science and supplies approaches the International Space Station for a docking on Sept. 19, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays. Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere . Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.

top.title: What we know about the 2035 UK Women's World Cup – and the questions that remain
top.description: It’s official: the 2035 Women’s World Cup belongs to the United Kingdom . This shouldn’t come as a surprise. England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland were the only bidders for the tournament, with the decision confirmed at a special FIFA meeting on Monday. Even so, the announcement is significant. The UK has not hosted a senior World Cup, men’s or women’s, since England staged (and won) the men’s edition in 1966. Nine years can feel like a long way away and, in the history of Women’s World Cup bidding rights, it is. Never before has a host nation for the women’s tournament been confirmed this far in advance. For the UK, it means time is both on the four home nations’ side and of the essence. The bid was clear in its expectations and ambitions: 104 matches, 48 teams, a potential 22 stadiums, 16 host cities, 4.5 million fans attending and 3.5 billion watching from their televisions around the globe. But what other ambitions does the UK have and what unknowns remain? The Athletic outlines the main talking points below. What do we know about dates and venues? Despite being the only bidders in the process, there are still many unknowns. Exact dates are to be confirmed, though we do know the tournament will consist of 104 matches over 39 days, with 48 teams competing (16 more than will be involved in next summer’s World Cup in Brazil). In the UK’s official bid, 19 venues were definitively included, the majority (14) of which are in England, with two from both Wales and Scotland and one in Northern Ireland. England’s venues are: Villa Park (Birmingham), the Amex (Brighton), Ashton Gate (Bristol), Elland Road (Leeds), Hill Dickinson Stadium (Liverpool), Emirates Stadium (London), Selhurst Park (London), Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (London), Wembley (London), Etihad Stadium (Manchester), St James’ Park (Newcastle), the City Ground (Nottingham), the Stadium of Light (Sunderland), and Old Trafford (Manchester). The Scotland venues are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road. Wales’ stadiums are Cardiff City Stadium and the Principality Stadium, both in Cardiff, while Northern Ireland’s Windsor Park (Belfast) is also included. Wembley is currently the only venue listed as a potential host for the competition’s final. However, that doesn’t mean other stadiums cannot still be a potential host venue — or even a venue for the final. In fact, Birmingham City’s new ground, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and any new Chelsea stadium can also be in the mix. No timeframe for when the stadiums must be finished has been provided, with such deadlines falling under FIFA’s jurisdiction, according to the Football Association’s director of women’s football, Sue Day. top.title: Dodgers notes – is it good Tarik Skubal signed elsewhere?
top.description: The biggest domino to fall this offseason fell Sunday, as Tarik Skubal signed with the New York Mets for 9 years, $450 million. The Los Angeles Dodgers did not even get to the point where they offered their playoffs starter a contract, as they were unwilling to go the number of years that Skubal was looking for. In her column on Monday, Mirjam Swanson of the L.A. Times argues that it is a good thing that the Dodgers missed out on the two-time Cy Young winner. As Swanson points out, Skubal is 30 years old and has already had three elbow surgeries. He will be 38 when his contract ends. And, as Swanson also pointed out, the Dodgers have eight starting pitchers without Skubal. They also have a stacked farm system should they feel the need to go out and trade for a starter at the deadline (should there be a season of which to have a deadline). Jim Swanson of the OC Register also ponders if its good that the Dodgers did not sign Skubal. He doesn’t beat around the bush, starting off by saying that the contract the Mets gave Skubal will not age well, because of the age of Skubal and his past injuries. Before this, Yoshinobu Yamamoto had the biggest contract for a pitcher, and as Swanson points out, he has more than lived up to his contact, in part bringing two World Series to the Dodgers, one of which he was the World Series MVP. Time will tell if this was a good move by Mets owner Steve Cohen or just be another one of his huge contracts that didn’t quite pan out. At least we know it’s not just the Dodgers “ruining baseball”.

top.title: When will the Red Sox pay someone $400M?
top.description: Boston, MA - October 5: Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy, chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and president Sam Kennedy attend an end-of-season press conference on October 5, 2026. (Photo by David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Major League Baseball could be undergoing some major changes over the next few months… I’d love to tell you folks that things are going to get figured out, but lying isn’t my bag and it looks extremely likely that we are just days away from a work stoppage, as the collective bargaining agreement between the MLBPA and the owners is set to expire on on Dec. 1. MLB commissioner Rob Manfred offered up a disheartening outlook on the situation last Wednesday, when he told reporters that the owners are adamant about instituting a salary cap that has been strongly opposed by the players’ union. MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer is being tasked with stopping the biggest fundamental change to the sport in decades, while also looking to impose changes that will allow players earlier freedom as the union is proposing expanded rosters, guidelines to protect against service time manipulation, and a soft floor that penalizes teams who don’t spend a certain amount. If you’re one of the millionaires, let me be the first to tell you that you’re not going to get everything you want. If you’re one of the billionaires, let me start by telling you to pound sand and continue by telling you that you, too, won’t be getting everything that you desire. I don’t have any clue as to what’s going to happen, but one question that has popped up in the final days of the current collective bargaining agreement is: How long it will take to see someone sign a $400 million deal with the Boston Red Sox. The New York Mets just handed out the fifth such contract in the history of the sport, when they agreed to terms with Tarik Skubal on Sunday. His new $450 million deal puts him in the same conversation as new teammate Juan Soto ($765M), old teammate Shohei Ohtani ($700M), Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ($500M), and Mike Trout ($426M). If a salary cap/floor is implemented, we could see the length of time between the most recent deal of that magnitude and the next deal of that magnitude greatly increase, but how does that impact the folks down at Four Jersey Street? The Red Sox don’t exactly seem eager to hand out $400 million, but they are just a few years removed from handing out $313 million to Rafael Devers. They were also said to be willing to pay an exorbitant amount of money to sign Soto, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Alex Bregman, Pete Alonso and other big name free agents in recent years. I don’t want to give them credit for ultimately cheaping out, but you would have to imagine there are circumstances that could see them eventually open up the pocket book — whether that be inflation, the presence of a salary cap and floor, or another once-in-a-lifetime talent who comes available and is willing to join them. top.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen and Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes meet after an NFL game on Dec. 10, 2023. (AP Photo/Ed Zurga) Copyright 2023 The Associated Press. All Rights Reserved The 6-5, 237-pound Josh Allen is a unique weapon who can make big plays with his arms or legs. But the Buffalo Bills quarterback did not have a single rushing attempt during Sunday’s victory against the Miami Dolphins. “That’s a setup,” Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo said. “They’ll have a good number of designed quarterback runs … We’re certainly going to be focused on quarterback runs and what he can do with the ball in his hands.” The Thanksgiving night game is setting up as another classic between two AFC heavyweights. Since Allen and Patrick Mahomes have become the starting quarterbacks for their respective teams, the Bills and Chiefs have met annually — and often times more than once — in every year, beginning in 2020. They are two of the best players in the NFL and are paid like it. In terms of contract value, Mahomes ranks first with a $504.75 million contract, and Allen is second with $330 million. But to prepare for Allen, the Chiefs used to turn to one of its bargain players on the practice squad. Quarterback Chris Oladokun used to impersonate mobile quarterbacks like Allen and Jalen Hurts, but Oladokun is now playing in the CFL. The Chiefs have not confirmed this, but one would think they have Justin Fields mimic Allen during their truncated week of practice. The athletic, 6-3, 227-pound Fields even ran for 1,143 yards and eight touchdowns during his second year in the NFL. The Allen-Mahomes Rivalry Since the Chiefs began playing against Allen, starting in 2020, Spagnuolo said Allen has developed into a more cerebral quarterback. And the Bills have won five consecutive regular-season meetings between the teams. They won during the 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022 and 2021 regular seasons, and the Chiefs won in the 2020 regular season. “He’s got this competitive nature about him,” Spagnuolo said, “where they’re going to somehow, someway will their team to win.” Though Allen has willed the Bills to win the regular-season contests between the teams, the rub is that the Chiefs have dominated the more important playoff games. top.title: Dolphins Defense Holds Ground While Offense Falters In Buffalo
top.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The team looked like a 1-8 squad for large parts of the afternoon, struggling to move the ball against a tough opponent. Even with a backup quarterback under center and an entire defensive line missing, the unit showed some fight before the offense gave up on them. According to Dolphins Talk , “You can’t expect that unit to do that for all 4 quarters without eventually cracking, especially when the offense is giving you no help, but kudos to Hafley for having the defense ready to play.” Stock Up for the Defense Chop Robinson has really improved his run game, showing he can stop the run while still rushing the passer. The linebacker is now a true four-down player who isn’t a liability against the run, which is a massive upgrade for the front seven. Jacob Rodriguez recorded double-digit tackles and made a big interception right before halftime to keep the score down. These players deserve credit for keeping the Dolphins in the game when the offense could not find a rhythm. The special teams unit, however, has been bad all year, and that trend continued on Sunday. Additionally, Chris Bell dropped a ball that hit him in the hands in the first half, a mistake that killed a potential drive. The source notes that this drop was critical because the offense needed every yard it could get. That is inexcusable, and the excuse “well, he is a rookie” won’t work in that situation. Stock Down for the Offense In the past 3 weeks, Caleb Douglas has dropped far too many passes, and this habit is now hurting the team’s chances to win close games. These drops are either bad luck or a failure of focus that the coaching staff must address immediately. top.title: Jayden Daniels may have cost Stefon Diggs a huge $250K bonus with Commanders snub
top.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs did not see eye to eye during the Washington Commanders’ win over the Cincinnati Bengals. Diggs was seen on camera chastising Daniels for not passing the ball to him when he was making runs that could have helped the Commanders advance the ball or even score touchdowns. The speech didn’t have much of an impact, as Daniels was unable to find Diggs in the right spots when needed, and in doing so, cost the WR a sizeable bonus. Stefon Diggs missed out on $250K bonus against Cincinnati Bengals thanks to Jayden Daniels Interestingly, prior to the game, one NFL news account reported that Stefon Diggs would have triggered a bonus clause in his Washington Commanders contract with two or more touchdowns against the Cincinnati Bengals. With $250K on the line, Diggs’ frustration with Daniels makes a lot more sense, as he saw the young QB’s failure as an act that was costing him a large sum of money. During the win against the Bengals, Diggs only had four receptions across six targets, receiving for only 45 yards. Compare this to WR Antonio Williams, whom Daniels found nine times across 11 attempts, allowing him to receive for 122 yards, and Diggs’ frustration becomes all the more justified. If it is even possible to give Diggs any consolation, Daniels failed to find any of his receivers on the night to throw for touchdowns, with the Commanders winning because of their success from field goal range. Diggs had a clause in his contract to receive a $250K incentive bonus for five or more touchdowns this season, a mark he has already hit. If he manages to catch two or more touchdowns in his next game, he will receive the second portion of that incentive bonus worth $250K, thus bringing his earnings through incentives to $500K for the season. top.title: Jamie Carragher says Chelsea have ‘no chance of achieving anything’ with current defence
top.description: Jamie Carragher has warned Chelsea they have “got absolutely no chance of achieving anything” with their current defensive options as he likened Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill to “kids”. Xabi Alonso ’s side were thumped 4-1 at home by rivals Leeds on Saturday and have conceded 20 goals in 11 Premier League games this season. With £52m summer signing Maxence Lacroix sidelined with a hamstring injury, Fofana and Colwill have been Alonso’s centre-back pairing for the Blues’ last three matches. Former Liverpool defender Carragher delivered a scathing assessment as he analysed Leeds’ equaliser, scored by Noah Okafor. “That is as bad as it gets in terms of conceding a goal in the Premier League,” Carragher said on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football. “You feel like you’re seeing kids playing in a men’s game. That’s the best way to describe it.” Only the bottom two, Crystal Palace and Manchester United, and promoted sides Ipswich and Coventry have worse defensive records than Chelsea. The Blues have lost three of their last four top-flight matches and are already 12 points adrift of leaders Arsenal and five behind fourth-placed Liverpool in the race for Champions League qualification. Levi Colwill (left) has struggled to get back to form since returning from injury (Reuters) “Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League,” said Carragher. “Lacroix is a decent player, that’s a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.” Chelsea were booed off by the home supporters who remained at Stamford Bridge after their thrashing by Leeds. The heavy defeat followed a 2-0 home loss to London rivals Tottenham and a 1-0 reverse at Sunderland , either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United . Xabi Alonso's side were booed off after defeat to Leeds (Getty) “Colwill at Sunderland against (Brian) Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time,” said Carragher. “Fofana’s performance against Manchester United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you’ll see from a centre-back this season. “As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.” Frenchman Fofana, 25, joined Chelsea in a £75m deal from Leicester in 2022, while 23-year-old Colwill came through the club’s academy and has been capped five times by England. “It almost feels like you’ve got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well,” added Carragher. Eighth-placed Chelsea return to action away to Nottingham Forest on Friday evening.

top.description: Nearly every fighter stepping into the ring at The Inner Circle 40 is chasing one of two things: a career-defining breakthrough or an immediate escape from a slide. Veteran Experience Meets Teenage Momentum In The Main Event Photo credit: ONE Championship Two generations of Thai striking collide in the main event, as two-time K-1 champion Yodkhunpon “Piranha Muangthai” squares off against 19-year-old phenom Detchawalit Silkmuaythai in bantamweight Muay Thai. One was forged in the championship rings of Thailand and Japan, while the other is just beginning his story — and racing through it at breakneck speed. top.title: Emmanuel Sanders predicts how many Super Bowls the 49ers will win in the next 10 years
top.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Former Super Bowl champion Emmanuel Sanders reveals how many Super Bowls he thinks the San Francisco 49ers will win in the foreseeable future. The San Francisco 49ers are tied with the Buffalo Bills for the best record in the NFL through 10 games. The team has lost just once, and they look like a serious Super Bowl contender yet again. Under head coach Kyle Shanahan, the Niners have made it all the way twice (in 2019 and 2023), but lost against the Kansas City Chiefs on both occasions. Quarterback Brock Purdy has been putting together an MVP campaign. The 26-year-old has a completion rate of 71 percent, has 23 touchdowns on the year to just five interceptions, and has an excellent 118.2 passer rating. His play and the team’s success have some former stars feeling good about the current iteration of the Niners. Emmanuel Sanders says San Francisco 49ers could win ‘two or three Super Bowls’ in 10 years Since Shanahan took over, the Niners have made the playoffs in five out of nine seasons. They have proven to be perennially dangerous, with only injuries causing their downfall in recent years. And while they aren’t over the hump yet, there is no reason to believe they won’t do it soon. Former 49ers star Emmanuel Sanders is a believer. He highlighted the duo of Purdy and Shanahan while expressing his confidence in the team’s ability to win a lot in the coming seasons. “Kyle Shanahan is a bad boy, you know, and it’s the reason why I sit back and say he’s a future Hall of Fame coach,” Sanders said. “Hey, look, I’m even jumping in. I think him and Purdy are going to win not just one, but multiple Super Bowls together, because Purdy is still young. Like I wouldn’t be surprised if they win two or three Super Bowls in the next 10 years with how they’re looking you know?” This is certainly a bold prediction, there are never any guarantees in the NFL. San Francisco has consistently fielded talented rosters in the 2020s, but it is yet to lead to Super Bowl success. If they do actually manage to win two or three in the next decade, it would be a huge success for Shanahan and the franchise. nigeria.title: Court nullifies Omo-Agege’s NDC senatorial candidacy, orders INEC to delist him

The court, presided over by Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates for the election and restrained the former Deputy Senate President from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate. In a further setback for the NDC, the court held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, noting that the Electoral Act prescribed a timeline of 180 days before the general elections. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary. Omo-Agege’s objection Delivering judgment, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit, before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff. The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act regarding the submission of its membership register to INEC ahead of its primary election. Justice Nganjiwa found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the conduct of the party’s primary election. The judge further held that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary. Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court also noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time. nigeria.title: Delta NDC Attack: IPAC warns against bloodshed ahead of 2027 elections
nigeria.description: The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) has called on the police and other security agencies to investigate the deadly attack on the campaign entourage of Sen. Ovie Omo-Agege in Delta, cautioning against further bloodshed. Mrs Temilola Akinade, Lagos State IPAC Chairperson, made the call while condemning the reported attack on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress. The NDC were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of the state when they were reportedly attacked. Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly elections. The IPAC chairperson called on political parties, leaders and their supporters to embrace tolerance, peaceful engagement and respect for democratic principles ahead of the 2027 General Elections. She also wished those injured in the attack a speedy and complete recovery. The IPAC chair reiterated that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to freedom of association, political participation and peaceful assembly without fear of intimidation or violence. nigeria.title: England Records 5,258 Heat-Linked Deaths This Summer- Health Agency
nigeria.description: England registered 5,258 deaths linked to this summer’s heat, the highest number of such fatalities on record, the UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said in estimates released Tuesday. “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer, with the highest mortality observed since 2016, when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports,” the agency said in a provisional report. Britain experienced its hottest summer on record this year, characterised by early and successive heatwaves. The country has also seen an exceptional drought that resulted from a lack of rainfall not seen in nearly 200 years. Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying extreme weather events, with Europe warming faster than the global average and heatwaves growing more frequent and severe. While the provisional figures may be revised, the mortality impact “exceeds that observed in any previous annual heat-associated mortality estimate”, the UKHSA added. People use emergency blankets to protect themselves from the heat as they arrive at the Olympic stadium for a concert of US singer Bruno Mars on June 28, 2026, in Berlin. (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) The latest figure, logged across seven “heat episodes” between May and September, topples the previous record of 2,985 estimated heat-linked deaths in summer 2022. The UKHSA analysis compares mortality during periods of heat with mortality during “nearby non-heat periods”, the agency said. This is particularly useful for understanding the impacts of heatwaves, it added. Multiple European countries registered record heat-related deaths after a sweltering summer this year, including Germany with 16,300 and more than 5,000 in Spain. A report published in The Lancet medical journal last month said climate change must be declared a “global health emergency” and found there were more than three million deaths caused by heat between 2016 and 2023. Tourists shield themselves from the sun with umbrellas at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican during a heatwave, on June 24, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP) Heat-related excess deaths often result from the higher risk of heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable. Britain’s national weather agency has predicted the El Nino weather pattern could make 2027 the hottest year globally. Experts are urging the country to better prepare homes and public infrastructure for warmer summers. nigeria.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for N65.17tn revised 2026 Budget
nigeria.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to repeal and reenact the 2026 Appropriation Act to the House of Representatives, proposing a revised federal expenditure of N65.176tn. The President also forwarded a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework to the House for consideration and approval. In a letter read on the floor of the House on Tuesday by the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu said the proposed adjustments were aimed at aligning the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure stands at N65.176tn, down from the N68.323tn approved in the original budget, while projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, is put at N33.720tn. The revised budget also provides for aggregate capital expenditure of N26.232tn, while retaining the fiscal deficit of N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product. Tinubu explained that the proposed adjustments would regularise some Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations and recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments. He said the revised framework would also provide for refunds to ministries, departments and agencies, as well as special accounts. According to the president, MDA capital provisions consist mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead provisions were introduced as priority national interventions. He listed the interventions to include the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability. On borrowing, the President said the planned new borrowing remained unchanged at N29.218tn, comprising N18.428tn in domestic borrowing and N10.790tn in foreign borrowing. He further disclosed that the proposed $7.7bn external borrowing, equivalent to approximately N10.368tn at an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the borrowing envelope. Tinubu said the adjustments were designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget and maintain fiscal restraint. He consequently appealed to the lawmakers for expeditious consideration and passage of the bill to facilitate the orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of outstanding obligations. nigeria.title: Nigeria can’t borrow its way out of economic crisis – Duke
nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Donald Duke, has warned that Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of its economic crisis, urging the federal government to shift from debt-driven spending to policies capable of expanding production, creating wealth and strengthening the country’s revenue base. Duke, who was former governor of Cross River State, spoke in an interview in Abuja against the backdrop of the country’s rising debt burden and persistent economic pressures on households and businesses. He said: “Borrowing is not inherently wrong, but the critical question is what borrowed funds were being used for and whether they were generating sufficient economic returns. “Nigeria cannot continue contracting loans simply to sustain an economic structure that is failing to produce enough wealth and revenue. “Borrowing could be justified where funds were invested in productive infrastructure and other ventures capable of expanding the economy, but not using debt to finance inefficiency or recurrent expenditure.” Duke said the country must instead focus on increasing productivity, improving the business environment and expanding the number of Nigerians and businesses participating meaningfully in the formal economy. The PRP presidential candidate argued that Nigeria’s fiscal challenge was ultimately a production problem. “A country that does not produce enough cannot generate the revenue required to meet its obligations, regardless of how much money it borrows. “There is a need for a fundamental review of government expenditure. Public funds should be directed towards investments that increase productivity, create employment and generate additional revenue. “Government should broaden the revenue base without imposing measures that further weaken households and businesses. “The objective should be to create an economy in which businesses grow, employment expands and government revenues increase naturally as economic activity increases. “Continuing to rely heavily on borrowing without addressing these structural weaknesses would simply shift today’s problems to future generations,”he warned. The former Cross River governor said Nigeria needed to move away from an economic model centered on finding money to sustain government towards one focused on creating wealth. He said the country did not merely need more money in government coffers but a stronger productive economy capable of generating the resources required to finance development. “As a presidential candidate, I am concerned not merely with managing the current economic crisis but with changing the underlying structure that repeatedly produces it. “Nigerians deserve an economic system capable of creating sustainable opportunities rather than one that continually responds to hardship after it has occurred,” he said. business.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. sports.title: What we know about the 2035 UK Women's World Cup – and the questions that remain
sports.description: It’s official: the 2035 Women’s World Cup belongs to the United Kingdom . This shouldn’t come as a surprise. England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland were the only bidders for the tournament, with the decision confirmed at a special FIFA meeting on Monday. Even so, the announcement is significant. The UK has not hosted a senior World Cup, men’s or women’s, since England staged (and won) the men’s edition in 1966. Nine years can feel like a long way away and, in the history of Women’s World Cup bidding rights, it is. Never before has a host nation for the women’s tournament been confirmed this far in advance. For the UK, it means time is both on the four home nations’ side and of the essence. The bid was clear in its expectations and ambitions: 104 matches, 48 teams, a potential 22 stadiums, 16 host cities, 4.5 million fans attending and 3.5 billion watching from their televisions around the globe. But what other ambitions does the UK have and what unknowns remain? The Athletic outlines the main talking points below. What do we know about dates and venues? Despite being the only bidders in the process, there are still many unknowns. Exact dates are to be confirmed, though we do know the tournament will consist of 104 matches over 39 days, with 48 teams competing (16 more than will be involved in next summer’s World Cup in Brazil). In the UK’s official bid, 19 venues were definitively included, the majority (14) of which are in England, with two from both Wales and Scotland and one in Northern Ireland. England’s venues are: Villa Park (Birmingham), the Amex (Brighton), Ashton Gate (Bristol), Elland Road (Leeds), Hill Dickinson Stadium (Liverpool), Emirates Stadium (London), Selhurst Park (London), Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (London), Wembley (London), Etihad Stadium (Manchester), St James’ Park (Newcastle), the City Ground (Nottingham), the Stadium of Light (Sunderland), and Old Trafford (Manchester). The Scotland venues are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road. Wales’ stadiums are Cardiff City Stadium and the Principality Stadium, both in Cardiff, while Northern Ireland’s Windsor Park (Belfast) is also included. Wembley is currently the only venue listed as a potential host for the competition’s final. However, that doesn’t mean other stadiums cannot still be a potential host venue — or even a venue for the final. In fact, Birmingham City’s new ground, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and any new Chelsea stadium can also be in the mix. No timeframe for when the stadiums must be finished has been provided, with such deadlines falling under FIFA’s jurisdiction, according to the Football Association’s director of women’s football, Sue Day. sports.title: Dodgers notes – is it good Tarik Skubal signed elsewhere?
sports.description: The biggest domino to fall this offseason fell Sunday, as Tarik Skubal signed with the New York Mets for 9 years, $450 million. The Los Angeles Dodgers did not even get to the point where they offered their playoffs starter a contract, as they were unwilling to go the number of years that Skubal was looking for. In her column on Monday, Mirjam Swanson of the L.A. Times argues that it is a good thing that the Dodgers missed out on the two-time Cy Young winner. As Swanson points out, Skubal is 30 years old and has already had three elbow surgeries. He will be 38 when his contract ends. And, as Swanson also pointed out, the Dodgers have eight starting pitchers without Skubal. They also have a stacked farm system should they feel the need to go out and trade for a starter at the deadline (should there be a season of which to have a deadline). Jim Swanson of the OC Register also ponders if its good that the Dodgers did not sign Skubal. He doesn’t beat around the bush, starting off by saying that the contract the Mets gave Skubal will not age well, because of the age of Skubal and his past injuries. Before this, Yoshinobu Yamamoto had the biggest contract for a pitcher, and as Swanson points out, he has more than lived up to his contact, in part bringing two World Series to the Dodgers, one of which he was the World Series MVP. Time will tell if this was a good move by Mets owner Steve Cohen or just be another one of his huge contracts that didn’t quite pan out. At least we know it’s not just the Dodgers “ruining baseball”.

sports.title: When will the Red Sox pay someone $400M?

MLB commissioner Rob Manfred offered up a disheartening outlook on the situation last Wednesday, when he told reporters that the owners are adamant about instituting a salary cap that has been strongly opposed by the players’ union. MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer is being tasked with stopping the biggest fundamental change to the sport in decades, while also looking to impose changes that will allow players earlier freedom as the union is proposing expanded rosters, guidelines to protect against service time manipulation, and a soft floor that penalizes teams who don’t spend a certain amount. If you’re one of the millionaires, let me be the first to tell you that you’re not going to get everything you want. If you’re one of the billionaires, let me start by telling you to pound sand and continue by telling you that you, too, won’t be getting everything that you desire. I don’t have any clue as to what’s going to happen, but one question that has popped up in the final days of the current collective bargaining agreement is: How long it will take to see someone sign a $400 million deal with the Boston Red Sox. The New York Mets just handed out the fifth such contract in the history of the sport, when they agreed to terms with Tarik Skubal on Sunday. His new $450 million deal puts him in the same conversation as new teammate Juan Soto ($765M), old teammate Shohei Ohtani ($700M), Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ($500M), and Mike Trout ($426M). If a salary cap/floor is implemented, we could see the length of time between the most recent deal of that magnitude and the next deal of that magnitude greatly increase, but how does that impact the folks down at Four Jersey Street? The Red Sox don’t exactly seem eager to hand out $400 million, but they are just a few years removed from handing out $313 million to Rafael Devers. They were also said to be willing to pay an exorbitant amount of money to sign Soto, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Alex Bregman, Pete Alonso and other big name free agents in recent years. I don’t want to give them credit for ultimately cheaping out, but you would have to imagine there are circumstances that could see them eventually open up the pocket book — whether that be inflation, the presence of a salary cap and floor, or another once-in-a-lifetime talent who comes available and is willing to join them. sports.title: Jayden Daniels may have cost Stefon Diggs a huge $250K bonus with Commanders snub
sports.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs did not see eye to eye during the Washington Commanders’ win over the Cincinnati Bengals. Diggs was seen on camera chastising Daniels for not passing the ball to him when he was making runs that could have helped the Commanders advance the ball or even score touchdowns. The speech didn’t have much of an impact, as Daniels was unable to find Diggs in the right spots when needed, and in doing so, cost the WR a sizeable bonus. Stefon Diggs missed out on $250K bonus against Cincinnati Bengals thanks to Jayden Daniels Interestingly, prior to the game, one NFL news account reported that Stefon Diggs would have triggered a bonus clause in his Washington Commanders contract with two or more touchdowns against the Cincinnati Bengals. With $250K on the line, Diggs’ frustration with Daniels makes a lot more sense, as he saw the young QB’s failure as an act that was costing him a large sum of money. During the win against the Bengals, Diggs only had four receptions across six targets, receiving for only 45 yards. Compare this to WR Antonio Williams, whom Daniels found nine times across 11 attempts, allowing him to receive for 122 yards, and Diggs’ frustration becomes all the more justified. If it is even possible to give Diggs any consolation, Daniels failed to find any of his receivers on the night to throw for touchdowns, with the Commanders winning because of their success from field goal range. Diggs had a clause in his contract to receive a $250K incentive bonus for five or more touchdowns this season, a mark he has already hit. If he manages to catch two or more touchdowns in his next game, he will receive the second portion of that incentive bonus worth $250K, thus bringing his earnings through incentives to $500K for the season. sports.title: Jamie Carragher says Chelsea have ‘no chance of achieving anything’ with current defence
sports.description: Jamie Carragher has warned Chelsea they have “got absolutely no chance of achieving anything” with their current defensive options as he likened Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill to “kids”. Xabi Alonso ’s side were thumped 4-1 at home by rivals Leeds on Saturday and have conceded 20 goals in 11 Premier League games this season. With £52m summer signing Maxence Lacroix sidelined with a hamstring injury, Fofana and Colwill have been Alonso’s centre-back pairing for the Blues’ last three matches. Former Liverpool defender Carragher delivered a scathing assessment as he analysed Leeds’ equaliser, scored by Noah Okafor. “That is as bad as it gets in terms of conceding a goal in the Premier League,” Carragher said on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football. “You feel like you’re seeing kids playing in a men’s game. That’s the best way to describe it.” Only the bottom two, Crystal Palace and Manchester United, and promoted sides Ipswich and Coventry have worse defensive records than Chelsea. The Blues have lost three of their last four top-flight matches and are already 12 points adrift of leaders Arsenal and five behind fourth-placed Liverpool in the race for Champions League qualification. Levi Colwill (left) has struggled to get back to form since returning from injury (Reuters) “Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League,” said Carragher. “Lacroix is a decent player, that’s a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.” Chelsea were booed off by the home supporters who remained at Stamford Bridge after their thrashing by Leeds. The heavy defeat followed a 2-0 home loss to London rivals Tottenham and a 1-0 reverse at Sunderland , either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United . Xabi Alonso's side were booed off after defeat to Leeds (Getty) “Colwill at Sunderland against (Brian) Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time,” said Carragher. “Fofana’s performance against Manchester United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you’ll see from a centre-back this season. “As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.” Frenchman Fofana, 25, joined Chelsea in a £75m deal from Leicester in 2022, while 23-year-old Colwill came through the club’s academy and has been capped five times by England. “It almost feels like you’ve got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well,” added Carragher. Eighth-placed Chelsea return to action away to Nottingham Forest on Friday evening.

sports.title: Emmanuel Sanders predicts how many Super Bowls the 49ers will win in the next 10 years
sports.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Former Super Bowl champion Emmanuel Sanders reveals how many Super Bowls he thinks the San Francisco 49ers will win in the foreseeable future. The San Francisco 49ers are tied with the Buffalo Bills for the best record in the NFL through 10 games. The team has lost just once, and they look like a serious Super Bowl contender yet again. Under head coach Kyle Shanahan, the Niners have made it all the way twice (in 2019 and 2023), but lost against the Kansas City Chiefs on both occasions. Quarterback Brock Purdy has been putting together an MVP campaign. The 26-year-old has a completion rate of 71 percent, has 23 touchdowns on the year to just five interceptions, and has an excellent 118.2 passer rating. His play and the team’s success have some former stars feeling good about the current iteration of the Niners. Emmanuel Sanders says San Francisco 49ers could win ‘two or three Super Bowls’ in 10 years Since Shanahan took over, the Niners have made the playoffs in five out of nine seasons. They have proven to be perennially dangerous, with only injuries causing their downfall in recent years. And while they aren’t over the hump yet, there is no reason to believe they won’t do it soon. Former 49ers star Emmanuel Sanders is a believer. He highlighted the duo of Purdy and Shanahan while expressing his confidence in the team’s ability to win a lot in the coming seasons. “Kyle Shanahan is a bad boy, you know, and it’s the reason why I sit back and say he’s a future Hall of Fame coach,” Sanders said. “Hey, look, I’m even jumping in. I think him and Purdy are going to win not just one, but multiple Super Bowls together, because Purdy is still young. Like I wouldn’t be surprised if they win two or three Super Bowls in the next 10 years with how they’re looking you know?” This is certainly a bold prediction, there are never any guarantees in the NFL. San Francisco has consistently fielded talented rosters in the 2020s, but it is yet to lead to Super Bowl success. If they do actually manage to win two or three in the next decade, it would be a huge success for Shanahan and the franchise. technology.title: CrowdStrike splashes $44B on Zscaler, customers brace for the bill
technology.description: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in what would be the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, and customers are already bracing for pricier renewals. The all-stock deal, announced on Monday , will see Zscaler shareholders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for every share they own, representing a 34 percent premium on Friday's closing price. The transaction dwarfs even Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security upstart Wiz . Buying Zscaler gives CrowdStrike a sizeable foothold in the network security market, where it will be going up against the likes of Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet. The plan is to combine Falcon's endpoint protection capabilities with Zscaler's zero-trust network security technology, giving customers a single platform for securing devices and the connections between them. Naturally, there's an AI angle to the biggest cyber deal in history. CrowdStrike reckons owning both technologies will allow it to keep tabs on what AI agents are doing on corporate devices, where they're connecting, and what data they're getting their hands on. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz described the proposed combination as "cybersecurity’s operating system." The acquisition also gives CrowdStrike's salespeople plenty to get excited about. Around 8,000 Zscaler customers don't currently buy CrowdStrike's wares, and the companies already have more than 2,000 customers in common. CrowdStrike reckons it can boost its annualized revenue by around $1 billion within 30 months of closing the deal by selling more products to the two companies' existing customers. Some of those customers, however, don't sound particularly keen on being cross-sold to. Over on Reddit's r/sysadmin subreddit, news of the purchase was met with a familiar set of concerns from IT professionals who've lived through big-ticket enterprise software acquisitions before. "As a zscaler customer, this does worry me. Cost increase, forced move to Falcon, integration issues, etc," wrote one sysadmin. Another, whose organization already uses both vendors' products, added: "I think they're both great products but I imagine they'll jack up the price for our next renewal. Fun." CrowdStrike intends to make Zscaler's products available through its Falcon Flex licensing scheme, which allows customers to commit to a certain level of spending and pick and choose the products they deploy. Monday's acquisition announcement didn't spell out what the deal would mean for customers who want to continue using Zscaler alongside a rival endpoint security product. Others raised concerns about the fate of Red Canary, the managed detection and response specialist snapped up by Zscaler in August 2025. CrowdStrike already operates a competing service in Falcon Complete. There may also be some nervous employees at both companies. technology.title: European Commission confirms personal data stolen in AI-assisted cyberattack
technology.description: The European Commission has confirmed that hackers made off with personal data in the AI-assisted cyberattack disclosed last week, but has relied on a website notice rather than contacting affected users directly. Speaking at a press briefing on Monday , Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed that EU Academy, an online learning platform offering courses on EU policies and initiatives, was among the systems compromised during the cyber campaign targeting the bloc's executive arm. The stolen data includes the names and email addresses of people outside the EU institutions, though the Commission has yet to figure out how many users are affected or whether other personal information was compromised. Public access to the platform has been disabled as a precaution. Despite confirming the theft, the Commission hasn't contacted affected individuals directly. Instead, it has posted a notice on the EU Academy website, a decision Regnier defended when quizzed by reporters on Monday. "There was no reach out to individual users, but rather a general message to all users on the website out of transparency," Regnier said. The notice warns users that they could find themselves on the receiving end of spearphishing attacks, impersonation attempts, and spam as a result of the breach. The Commission is also advising users not to hand over personal information to anyone who contacts them claiming to be involved in EU Academy activities. The trouble with notifying users via the EU Academy website is that they've already been told not to come back until January. A separate notice says the platform will be offline from November 11 through January 14, 2027, while the Commission rebuilds it. When it reopens, users will have to register again, and any record of their previous coursework won't be transferred. The Register has asked the Commission whether the downtime and the requirement to create new accounts are connected to the cyberattack.A spokesperson didn't answer those points. The Commission has informed the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS), the watchdog responsible for policing EU institutions' handling of personal data. The EDPS told The Register that the Commission had notified it of the incident in stages, but declined to say whether it considered the Commission's approach to notifying affected users sufficient. "I can confirm that the EDPS has been informed and notified in phases by the European Commission," a spokesperson said. "Our colleagues remain in regular contact with EC services on the cyberattack and its implication. This is an ongoing case, so I cannot tell you more at this stage on the actions the EDPS might take as supervisory authority." The Commission first publicly acknowledged the cyberattack last Thursday , almost a month after suspicious activity was detected on October 22. technology.description: The British government is investing in a UK-based AI defense startup that aims to train autonomous military systems in virtual environments, in a bid to reduce the country's reliance on overseas technology. Both the Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF) have contributed to a Series A funding round for Agon Dynamics, said to value the biz at $450 million. technology.title: Education software supplier's legacy login system left 355,000 school email addresses exposed
technology.description: More than 355,000 school staff and pupil email addresses ended up in the hands of hackers who broke into UK education software supplier Bromcom in September. The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on Monday, revealing that 355,051 unique email addresses were caught up in the incident. The data also included single sign-on (SSO) registration reference numbers, although Bromcom insists that no passwords or authentication tokens were stolen. As The Register reported in Octobe r , the attackers got in through a legacy SSO registration component in Bromcom's Communications Server environment. The technology had already been superseded but was still running because an internal system continued to use it. Bromcom discovered something was amiss on September 6 after customers reported problems accessing its SSO service. At the time, the company was still working with external forensic specialists to establish exactly what the intruders had managed to get their hands on. Bromcom's FAQ says its investigation is complete and confirms that the intruders used a script to extract SSO registration information from the compromised server. The supplier insists its Management Information System (MIS), used by schools to keep track of everything from attendance to pupil records, was untouched. The compromised service also couldn't be used to get into Microsoft or Google accounts, which have their own login systems. Bromcom has since pulled the plug on the old component, tightened its authorization checks, and added more security logging. It says it hasn't found any evidence of accounts being hijacked as a result of the breach. Bromcom also confirmed it hadn't reported the breach to the UK's Information Commission's Office. Its reasoning is that it was the data processor, not the controller, so any decision to involve the regulator was for the affected schools and academy trusts to make. As for the risk to staff and pupils, Bromcom considers it to be low. No passwords or pupil records held in the MIS were taken, it says, although schools have been advised to watch for phishing messages and suspicious requests to reset passwords or approve sign-ins. The supplier's software is used by more than 5,000 schools and 390 multi-academy trusts across the UK, though it hasn't said how many were caught up in this particular mess. The Register has asked Bromcom how many schools and pupils were affected, and whether the figure published by Have I Been Pwned matches its own findings, but has yet to receive a response. Bromcom kept the superseded component running because an internal system still needed it. Unfortunately, the intruders found a use for it too. ®

technology.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
technology.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. science.title: Russia launches Progress cargo ship to the International Space Station
science.description: null Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station. The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long. The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module. The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019. Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com. Progress 96 cargo spacecraft packed with science and supplies approaches the International Space Station for a docking on Sept. 19, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays. Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere . Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.
